bullets.title: NVDA +8.5% post-earnings: FY28 +70% guide vs. ~45% consensus stuns markets
bullets.body: Nvidia surged ~8.5% adding $435-500B in market cap after guiding FY28 revenue growth of 70% y/y versus street expectations of ~45%; management noted demand would be >100% growth if supply were unconstrained. Q2 revenue came in at $96B (+106% YoY) with ~75% gross margins and ~$60B net income. Raymond James raised PT to $515 (Strong Buy); Evercore to $465; Bernstein to $400; analyst noted 79% probability NVDA ends year as world's largest company.

bullets.title: Tech +3.4% on AI monetization narrative; rest of market red (10 of 11 sectors down)
bullets.body: S&P 500 finished up ~80bps but with deeply negative breadth — 10 of 11 sectors declined while tech gained ~3%. Software had its best session since April 2025 (IGV+); the software vs. semis basket hit a 4-month high and is up 70% from June lows. The AI disruption narrative is flipping to AI monetization as earnings evidence stacks up.

bullets.title: Fed's Hammack calls for rate hikes now; sees inflation stuck near 3% by year-end
bullets.body: Cleveland Fed President Hammack stated 'now is the time to act' on persistent inflation, expressing concern that Fed policy is not currently restrictive enough. She sees inflation easing to 2.5% 'at best' next year and warned of an inflationary mindset forming. KC Fed's Schmid separately flagged long-term credibility risk if the Fed is not seen as serious on inflation. OIS pricing 30% probability of a September hike; markets pricing zero cuts in 2026 at 88% odds.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole kicks off Friday: Warsh speech at 10am ET, market expects limited volatility
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday at 10am ET on 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy' with no Q&A, limiting potential for outsized market reaction. JPM notes positioning is less stretched than prior FOMC meetings. Key scenarios: if Warsh walks back doubts on Fed funds rate efficacy → curve flattening (bearish); if he emphasizes supply-side productivity → curve steepening (dovish). 5Y yield technical support near 4.50%.

bullets.title: July goods trade deficit blows out to $118.8B, widest since March 2025
bullets.body: The advance goods trade deficit surged 17.2% to $118.8B in July, far above the $100.5B consensus, as real imports rose 4.1% (capital goods +11%) while real exports fell 1.6% for a second straight month. Morgan Stanley lowered its 3Q GDP tracking estimate to 1.8% from 2.2%; Goldman lowered its 3Q GDP tracker by 0.1pp to 2.7%.

bullets.title: Initial jobless claims drop to 203K, labor market stays tight
bullets.body: Initial claims fell to 203K versus 208K consensus and the prior week's 207K; continuing claims also beat at 1.778M vs. 1.792M estimate. Data suggests the labor market remains resilient despite broader macro uncertainty and is inconsistent with an AI-driven employment apocalypse.

bullets.title: US corporate profits surged 9.1% in Q2, up 23% YoY; pretax margins near historic highs
bullets.body: US resident corporations' before-tax global profits rose 9.1% in Q2 2026 and are up 23% vs. four quarters ago. Nonfinancial domestic after-tax margins reached an all-time record high, with labor's share of net value added declining and fixed costs well-behaved. Fiscal deficit continues to provide structural support to the profit environment.

bullets.title: SaaS sector bifurcation, not collapse: infrastructure estimates up $21.5B, apps down $10.5B
bullets.body: KeyBanc notes the 'SaaS Death Index' is up 38.4% in 3 months versus 'SaaS Killers' down 3.6%, validating a sector bottom. Applications software bookings estimates for 2026-28 fell $10.5B while infrastructure software estimates rose $21.5B — the market is differentiating winners from losers rather than selling the category wholesale. Salesforce's Q2 results, described as the 'strongest evidence' that enterprise AI creates bifurcation not collapse, reinforced the thesis.

bullets.title: AWS ordering 2M incremental Nvidia GPUs for 2027-28; Anthropic commits $45B to Nscale
bullets.body: AWS is purchasing multiple million additional Nvidia GPUs for 2027-2028 even as it ramps its own Trainium2/3/4 chips (1M+ already deployed). Separately, Anthropic signed a $45B, six-year deal with Nscale for 460MW of compute capacity at a West Virginia data center. Meta is projected to spend up to $10B/year on Anthropic AI tools per NYT. AI infrastructure spending visibility now extends through 2028.

bullets.title: NVDA reportedly acquiring Hugging Face for ~$12.9B, expanding open-source AI platform control
bullets.body: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for approximately $12.9B, which would extend its dominance from hardware into the center of the open-source AI model and dataset ecosystem. Neither company has publicly confirmed the deal. NVDA also launched NVPAC, an employee-funded political action committee, signaling increased political engagement.

bullets.title: Memory shortage seen persisting through 2030; SK Hynix breaks ground on $4B Indiana fab
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO stated the memory shortage is expected to continue through 2030 at a groundbreaking ceremony for the company's $4B advanced packaging facility in Indiana. Analysts note HBM, DRAM, and NAND are distinct markets that should not be conflated in cycle analysis. MRVL specifically guided acceleration in custom ASIC and networking in H2 FY27.

bullets.title: AI data center 2027 demand tracking ~2x deliverable supply; power is the binding constraint
bullets.body: Analysis from DeepAIDC projects North American AI data center IT demand in 2027 at ~35GW versus only 16.5-23.4GW of deliverable supply, with power availability — not capital — as the binding constraint. DC construction also faces political/regulatory headwinds in Ohio, TX, and PA, causing buyers to frontload compute hardware while deferring other infrastructure components.

bullets.title: 7Y Treasury auction clears at 4.512% on-the-screws despite declining foreign demand
bullets.body: The 7-year Treasury auction priced at 4.512%, matching the when-issued level despite a notable decline in indirect (foreign) bidder participation. Yields finished the day up 1-2bps across the curve; the bond market is resisting Treasury Secretary Bessent's efforts to lower US borrowing costs amid sticky inflation concerns.

bullets.title: NY Fed MCT core PCE fell to 2.67% in August, suggesting underlying inflation may be moderating
bullets.body: The NY Fed Multivariate Core Trend PCE peaked at 3.50% in April and has fallen each month since, reaching 2.67% in August 2026. Unlike Trimmed Mean, MCT tends to lead inflation signals rather than lag, suggesting underlying price pressures may be easing ahead of official reads.

bullets.title: Software vs. semis sector rotation: momentum fleeing memory into software names
bullets.body: Multiple sources note a rotation dynamic with the software vs. semis basket at a 4-month high and up 70% from June lows. Hedgeye reports software longs up 32-78% since May 26 vs. IGV ETF +9%. Memory stocks including Micron have not kept pace with NVDA's post-earnings gain; analysts are questioning the cycle-peak thesis for MU/SNDK given distinct HBM/DRAM/NAND dynamics.

bullets.title: Foreign investors bought record $800B+ in US equities over past year
bullets.body: Foreign investors have purchased more than $800 billion in US stocks over the past year, representing the largest historical foreign investment in US equities. The S&P 500 is up 33% YTD while international markets have dramatically outperformed (South Korea +258%, Peru +147%).

bullets.title: Hormuz tensions ease; oil at $83/bbl; US-Venezuela oil deal talks ongoing
bullets.body: Risk premiums around the Strait of Hormuz are easing after Iran-Oman discussions on a temporary shipping corridor, with Brent crude pulling back ~3.9% to $88.58 earlier but WTI later extending gains above $83/bbl. Separately, the Trump administration is in talks with Venezuela's interim government for a stake in Venezuelan oil fields, potentially benefiting PADD 3 refiners.

bullets.title: Meta faces $17B child addiction settlement; Trump AI SRO executive order stalls
bullets.body: Meta agreed to a $17B settlement over claims it addicted children to Instagram and Facebook. Separately, a draft Trump executive order to create an AI self-regulatory organization has stalled amid opposition from tech advisers. Meta is projected to spend up to $10B/year on Anthropic models despite the legal liability, and the EU is awaiting proposals from Meta.

bullets.title: VIX at one-week low of 15.04; SPY $1.1B call wall at 770 with bulls in technical control
bullets.body: The CBOE VIX hit a one-week low of 15.04 as NVDA earnings lifted sentiment. Options flow showed $1.1B in calls positioned at SPY 770 with bulls described as in control above that level; NVDA alone saw >$200M in bullish options flow on the day. Equal-weight S&P lagged market-cap-weighted by >100bps, highlighting the narrow rally leadership.

bullets.title: Prediction markets: Claude favored as top LLM at 73%; 56% odds of Fed rate hike in 2026
bullets.body: StreetAccount prediction markets show Claude (Anthropic) favored as best AI model by year-end at 73% vs. ChatGPT 14%, Grok 9%, Gemini 8%. On monetary policy, markets price 56% odds of a Fed rate hike in 2026, 88% probability of zero cuts, and only 9% odds of US recession by year-end. Tariff increase odds on Canada fell to 20% week-over-week.
